description.narrative: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, human rights violations are widespread and human security is far from guaranteed. Violations and abuses, by both state and non-state actors, include extrajudicial killings, arbitrary arrests, torture and sexual violence against women and girls. Democratic space is restricted with far_x0002_reaching consequences for press, civil society organisations and human rights defenders active on issues like natural resources, human rights, accountability and elections monitoring.

The activity is part of a larger programme implemented by the Strengthening Civil Courage Alliance, consisting of ABAAD – Resource Center for Gender Equality, Amnesty International The Netherlands, DefendDefenders, PAX and their partner networks.

The programme aspires to contribute to improving the human rights and human security situation at different levels. It aims to support pro_x0002_democratic civil society actors in effectively advocating for the improvement of electoral laws, institutions and processes. At the same time, it works with local organisations and selected communities in East and Northeast Congo on resolving (armed) conflict and the protection of human rights by state and non-state authorities. Conflicts relate for instance to access to land and natural resources and may e.g. occur between communities and authorities, between nomadic and resident communities or between artisanal miners and industrial mining companies. Activities include skills development (including on physical and digital security), monitoring and documenting human rights violations, facilitating dialogues and advocacy campaigns.

The programme primarily works with (women) human rights defenders, pro-democratic civil society actors, and with selected local communities affected by natural reserves policies, industrial mining or violent conflict with rival groups.

title.narrative: outcome 1.1. Partner organisations have a joint lobbying and advocacy agenda and coordinated strategy towards free and fair elections.
# of (joint) advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs on electoral reform for, by or with their membership/ constituency (SCS 4)

comment.narrative: Currently the government seems to intend to postpone the elections, to hamper electoral reform and the government does not respect the political independence of the electoral institutions and corresponding legal authorities. The joint strategies and interventions between our partner organisations and the christian churches did not take place yet at the beginning of this programme.
5 joint advocacy initiatives conducted by partners for electoral reform/ free and fair elections

2021: 1 advocacy initiative at a national level, consisting of 1) Public agreeement ECC and CENCO on electoral process 16th september; 2) Joint Conference and joint declaration ECC-CENCO and constituency (15-16 September); 3) Collaboration CLC-MILAPRO-CALCC on public manifestation november; 4) 8 joint declaration CALCC-MILAPRO on electroal process. 1 initiative at an international level consisting of 1) 6 meetings PAX with EU embassies (June, July, November); 2) Lobby meeting ECC-CENCO-PAX and 8 embassies; 3) 3 bilateral lobby meetings CALCC-MILAPRO-PAX with embassies; 4) 2 Policy Briefs on the electoral process by PAX, published by EURAC ; 5) 6 lobby meetings PAX and staff EURAC with EU institutions and EU embassies on policy briefs. 2022: Two partner organizations, tied to the Catholic and Protestant churches, coordinated their advocacy initiatives with regards to the electoral process. This coordination was endorsed by these Christian organizations’ hierarchies. In 2022, this happened through several meetings, an international conference on the electoral process organized by a European NGO network in Kinshasa, and one high-profile sit-in. The two partner organizations organized this sit-in in August 2022 in front of the US Embassy on the occasion of the visit of US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, with the participation also of leaders of the 'Social and political forces' movement. They handed out a memo and had high-level direct advocacy meetings with embassy staff before and after the sit-in. In the following months, the US government made public statements on the electoral process in line with our partners’. An estimated one thousand participants, including women and youth, participated in these activities. The partners’ spokespeople also frequently appeared in the media, calling for free and fair elections, and cautioning against substandard elections. A challenge to implement this initiative was the difficulty to mobilize large crowds of Congolese people around the elections in 2022 for several reasons: many Congolese still feel disillusioned after the elections fraud of 2018; many focused on what they considered more urgent and pressing issues, such as food insecurity, insecurity in urban areas, and armed conflict in the east; the fact that the election date (December 2023) still seemed relatively distant. The alliance between Catholic and Protestant lay organizations and coordination on the issue of elections was highlighted by key actors as innovative and important to maintain for achieving impact as the elections date approaches. 2023: Lobby initiative involving PAX and the EurAc network (composed of Europe-based NGOs working on Central Africa). This resulted among others in 2 publications with recommendations on the electoral process: a statement issued on 25 May 2023 and another one published on 14 December 2023.

title.narrative: Output 2.5.4. lobby at a national (Ministry of the Environment) and international level (donors of Park Lomami) to support the dialogue process and accept its outcomes
# of advocacy initiatives carried out by CSOs for, by or with their membership/ constituency in support of dialogue process to resolve conflict in Lomami Park (SCS4)

comment.narrative: HQ of state organization ICCN (institute for national reserves) has signed an agreement with partner organization CdjP-Kisangani and PAX that authorizes the start of an official dialogue process with the local ICCN office in Kindu and the communities surrounding the natural reserve Lomami.
15 lobby and advocacy interventions regarding conflict in Lomami Park

2022: This consisted in advocacy meetings with the national park and other actors tied to it, including development agencies, foreign embassies, and international and national NGOs with programmes in the park and its buffer zone. The purpose of these meetings was to gain support for our dialogue initiative, better gauge the international players’ positions on issues related to Lomami Park, and gather additional information on the park’s history and recent developments. The fact that the director of the park left in late 2022 requires additional engagement with the new head. This process is complex, partly because the park and its buffer zone cover a large zone, spread over 3 provinces; each area has its own specificities and tensions. Instead of one main dialogue covering general issues linked to the park-local communities relations, it now seems to make more sense to hold a series of dialogues at more local levels (level of the ‘territoires’ or lower), to take into account local particularities and to bring the dialogues closer to the affected communities. 2023: In 2023, PAX and CDJP-Kis focused on the local and provincial levels, without active lobbying at the national or international levels.

title.narrative: Outcome 3.3. EU improves the due diligence regulation on natural resources (3TGold legislation) and its implementation on an upstream level
# of laws, policies blocked, adopted, improved for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement (EU 3TGold (conflict minerals) - SCS2

comment.narrative: No adaptations of the 3TGold Regulations so far; new due diligence legislation in the making (EU and member state level)
EU has improved its 3TGold (conflict minerals) due diligence Regulation on the import of gold from conflict countries such as the DR Congo and has improved the implementation of the Regulation.

2021: The reporting on the shortcomings of the implementation of the 3TGold Regulation at a member state level, will be included in the EU evaluation of the Regulation in 2023. 2022: No adaptations of the 3TGold Regulations so far. 2023: PAX published a report (with IPIS) and participated in advocacy to improve the EU 'Conflict minerals' or '3TG' regulation. While this fed the debates, it did not lead in 2023 to substantial change with this regulation.

title.narrative: # of CSOs included in SPs (Strategic Partners) programmes

comment.narrative: One PAX partner organisation is a grass root level organisation with very strong ties with the local communities and local (customary) authorities. They have credibility among their constituency in the province of Haut Uele for the different issues they work on. Their relationships at a national and an international level are channeled through the work of PAX. Another PAX partneri is a faith-based grass root level organisation linked to the Diocese of Kisangani. But they are part of a national network and can count on support of the national umbrella organisation. The partner has credibility among the catholic base and good relationships at a local level. Their staff and administrative capacity is limited. Another PAX partner is an alliance of both catholic faith based groups and the constituency of the protestant churches at a national level. Most interventions take place in Kinshasa but the presence of the organisations is nationwide. The alliance is linked to the council of protestant churches and to the Catholic Bishop's Conference. Their main focus is on the elections and their strategies focus on civic activism and lobby and advocacy. The two partners in North-Kivu are specializing in MDR, with AINL’s support. They are linking up with advocacy and lobby activities in the region, to make sure lobby and advocacy is evidence-based.

For the PAX partners, the partnership would evolve in such a way that partner organisations are open to collaborate with other organisations that have impact in their field, so their impact of their work would increase and the depence of PAX would decrease. As for AINL, the partner portfolio does not need changing. Instead, links with existing lobby and advocacy platforms are strengthened.

2 AINL partners participate in divers alliances related to the defense of human rights. Furthermore, they create alliances with local alliances and other CSO representative in panels that meet regularly to discuss the human rights violations and abuses documented by their monitors. The partners are very succesful in advocacy on community level and aim to strenthen their capacities in bringing their issues to provincial and national levels by strengthening contacts with authortities (I)NGOs and embassies.
2 PAX partners work on civic education and non violent action around the electoral process. 1 PAX partner works on conflicts related to the presence of Mbororo herders, the LRA, and gold mining.1 PAX partner works on a dialogue between the Lomami National Park and surrounding communities. We would like to see these partners further strengthen their institutional capacities and collaborate more often with other NGOs, including by playing leading roles in civil society networks. We hope that they will improve women’s meaningful participation in decision-making processes. We also encourage them to liaise with other potential partners/donors, as to decrease dependency on PAX.

We are currently strengthening the partner organisations on research and MDR skills (AINL), as well as their lobby and advocacy capacities. During current programming period the partners will become more autonomous in the implementation of those interventions and our partnerships can focus more on complementary interventions of the partner organisations on the one hand and the alliance partners on the other. The current strengthening process of their institutional capacities will eventually lead to more financial independence of the alliance partners. Pax will explore possibilities for partnerships with specific and complementary expertise on environmental issues related to conflicts.

The partners in 2023 were NGOs and faith-based organizations based in the capital, Kinshasa, as well as in the east and northeast of the DRC. They all are inclusive of youth and women but are not youth- or women-led. In 2024, the parner folio in the DRC will be largely similar, but without the Kinshasa-based partner (with whom the partnership was about the period before the December 2023 elections). Continuing with the same partners, and building on what has already been done, will greatly help with efficacy as the programme enters in its two final years.

For the PAX partners, the partnership would evolve in such a way that partner organisations are open to collaborate with other organisations that have impact in their field, so the impact of their work would increase and the dependance of PAX would decrease. As for AINL, the partner portfolio does not need changing. Instead, links with existing lobby and advocacy platforms are strengthened.

The status of two PAX partner organisations is permanent as we have continious programming with them and invest the strengthening of ther instiitutional and political capacity. They have specific sections for women, but women's meaningful participation in the decision-making process can be improved. Three PAX partner organisations are all working on the electoral issue and are all three faith based organsiations. We want to itensify the relationship with those organisations during the coming two years (elections 2023) and improve the collaboration between them and with the partner organisations of our network.
